author: Patrick Xjr
text:
Good morning 
In fact as said before the measures aren’t the same but the most important is how you monitor, adapting your meals, making physical training in order to decrease peeks in size and frequency. The sensor helps you for understanding what your pancreas is doing in terms of insuline. For sure it isn’t a on/off system. Normally if you compare your blood analysis Hba1c and gpi on app values are comparable at 0.2 or 0.3 is difference.
Then when you install a new sensor there is is a couple of hours with values not so accurate (time for sensor to calibrate.)
But the main target is adapting your way of life in order to avoid peeks over 180 mg and almost to not to be under 70 mg (hypo).
Good luck
Patrick

author: Stephanie Maniatis
text:
Remember they aren’t measuring the same exact thing - blood vs interstitial fluid.

Also the IF is usually 20 minutes behind blood.

Blood is the gold standard, good on the hospital for requiring it.

Also sensors have an acceptable 20% margin of error.

author: Elaine Osbon Sullivan
text: Stephanie Maniatis This!  The CGM is around 15 minutes ahead of finger sticks, so it shouldn’t always be the same. Plus, I see posts all the time where someone is getting different numbers from finger sticks when done back to back.  7 points is nothing
